notes: Nigeria Hardening I + II Adoption Gates. Hardening I border-cash claims (NG-CUST-* / NG-NGN-01) preserved. Hardening II adds NG-ACC-01..16 from M2.5-reviewed ACC candidates. Does not draft data/rules/nigeria.json. Legacy resident-approval and non-resident 'more freely' formulations are excluded via forbidden inferences. FX Manual 2026 operational domiciliary rules remain unresolved (NG-ACC-13 temporal only, unbound).

claims.subject: Entry cash / negotiable-instrument declaration (statutory)
claims.rule: Transportation of cash or negotiable instruments in excess of US$10,000 or its equivalent by individuals into Nigeria shall be declared to the Nigeria Customs Service
claims.scope: border entry; cash or negotiable instruments; individual travellers
claims.authority: Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-001; reviewed fingerprint sha256:192062fcdd12413970f59aa55f510fb2e77dd2d882dadbffaabf86dde2d69323; MLPPA 2022 s.3(3) entry limb; statutory operator remains 'in excess of' (>), not >=
forbidden_inferences: declaration threshold is a carrying ceiling

claims.subject: Exit cash / negotiable-instrument declaration (statutory)
claims.rule: Transportation of cash or negotiable instruments in excess of US$10,000 or its equivalent by individuals out of Nigeria shall be declared to the Nigeria Customs Service
claims.scope: border exit; cash or negotiable instruments; individual travellers
claims.authority: Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-002; reviewed fingerprint sha256:6a23f5bb209722fd816938be92968dfa51a7ed47e65c1c57d19bb9c54b94ab52; MLPPA 2022 s.3(3) exit limb; statutory operator remains 'in excess of' (>); does not establish a general outbound carriage ceiling
forbidden_inferences: amount declared on entry as universal outbound ceiling
declaration threshold is a carrying ceiling

claims.subject: False or failed cash declaration offence consequence
claims.rule: Any person who falsely declares or fails to make a declaration to the Nigeria Customs Service under section 12 of the Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act commits an offence and is liable on conviction to forfeit the undeclared funds or negotiable instrument or to imprisonment for a term of at least two years or both
claims.scope: border entry or exit declaration failure / false declaration
claims.authority: Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-003; reviewed fingerprint sha256:ab5cd17b7b4429656ce75a781b742940edfd83e6d8ae503504da779e4e252e66; uses M2.5 reviewed_text restoring statutory 'liable on conviction' (not softened 'may lead'); MLPPA 2022 s.3(4)-(5) pinpoint; Customs-to-CBN reporting chain not adopted
allowed_wording: imprisonment for a term of at least two years

claims.subject: Declaration rule is not itself a prohibition on genuine funds above threshold
claims.rule: The reviewed official CBN guidance states that the declaration rule for cash or negotiable instruments above US$10,000 does not itself prohibit genuinely owned or obtained funds above that amount from being brought into Nigeria or taken outside the country
claims.scope: border entry or exit; declaration vs prohibition distinction only
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-004; reviewed fingerprint sha256:2ce7ee95f4585498c81401675b5951278c6afb3fbe52c4f9e4c06099665df3d2; CBN 2013 clarification; narrow negative only — does not establish unrestricted carriage or absence of other Nigerian-law limits
forbidden_inferences: no ceiling exists under all Nigerian law
foreign currency can be taken without limit

claims.subject: Imported cash domiciliary-account withdrawal / re-export condition (FEMMPA s.21)
claims.rule: Where a person imports foreign currency in excess of US$10,000 or its equivalent in cash and not by means of a bank draft, mail or telegraphic transfer and deposits the foreign currency in a domiciliary account with an authorised dealer, withdrawals from that account may be made only in cash, and that imported cash is exportable from Nigeria only in cash
claims.scope: imported cash deposited in a domiciliary account with an authorised dealer; cash-not-transfer condition retained
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-005; reviewed fingerprint sha256:bcb07b851173383e58f1b9506e2a5bff697bf4c9cf260009276a2c11582c34ba; FEMMPA 1995 s.21(1)-(2) with restored cash-not-transfer condition; not a universal outbound traveller rule
allowed_wording: not by means of a bank draft, mail or telegraphic transfer
exportable from Nigeria only in cash
forbidden_inferences: outbound foreign currency is limited to amount declared on entry
every departing traveller requires authorised-dealer documentation
s.21 establishes a universal outbound carriage ceiling

claims.subject: Customs e-CDF operational declaration trigger
claims.rule: Current Customs operational guidance on the e-currency declaration form uses a declaration trigger of US$10,000 or more / equal to or greater than US$10,000
claims.scope: Nigeria Customs Service e-CDF operational guidance; does not amend statutory MLPPA operator
claims.authority: Nigeria Customs Service
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-006; reviewed fingerprint sha256:1f35bc49455e3c7d3fcfb1dd33691747b4fc36565474e06a59c43004cbd59715; operational operator >= only; Hardening I-B dual-operator preservation vs MLPPA > remains; Customs >= does not formally amend statutory >
allowed_wording: equal to or greater than US$10,000

claims.subject: Legacy FEMMPA s.12 US$5,000 statistical declaration threshold
claims.rule: FEMMPA 1995 section 12 states that foreign currency in excess of US$5,000 or its equivalent, whether being imported into or exported out of Nigeria, shall be declared on the prescribed form for reasons of statistics only. That older threshold wording is retained for temporal audit and must not drive the current border-cash declaration threshold while MLPPA 2022 section 3(3) uses in excess of US$10,000
claims.scope: temporal audit only; not a current traveller threshold
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-CASH-007; reviewed fingerprint sha256:12725ae59a82f23f97f1e9634f61792af23d42fcb1941c394a58bd67e318b864; historical/superseded role; must not enter current-rule field bindings
forbidden_inferences: travellers must declare above US$5,000 under current AML law

claims.subject: Physical naira import/export prohibition baseline
claims.rule: The importation and exportation of the naira remain prohibited except as permitted under guidelines issued from time to time by the Central Bank
claims.scope: cross-border physical naira notes; prohibition baseline only; current numeric traveller exception not established in this review
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-NGN-001; reviewed fingerprint sha256:165c2cb6d5132261f2a369c6a7a9b85479332030df92d9cca1bcb86334223647; FEMMPA 1995 s.14; Hardening I-B numeric exception not established — do not invent N10,000 / N20,000 / N100,000
allowed_wording: importation and exportation of the naira remain prohibited
current numeric traveller exception not established
forbidden_inferences: travellers may carry NGN up to a stated numeric limit

claims.subject: Domiciliary account opening with Authorised Dealer
claims.rule: Any person may open, maintain and operate a domiciliary account designated in foreign currency with an Authorised Dealer
claims.scope: foreign-currency domiciliary account; Authorised Dealer; statutory opening/maintenance/operation only
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-001; reviewed fingerprint sha256:c8b1b54aedcc50a17c9e7cd773eaf5467c68508974e3b8474caf7e59bfdd9700; FEMMPA 1995 s.17(1)
allowed_wording: open, maintain and operate a domiciliary account
forbidden_inferences: prior CBN approval required to open domiciliary account

claims.subject: Domiciliary account convertible-currency denomination
claims.rule: The foreign currency in which a domiciliary account may be opened, maintained and operated shall be any internationally convertible currency
claims.scope: domiciliary-account denomination only; not funding, withdrawal, conversion, or transfer rights
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-002; reviewed fingerprint sha256:399d83763c0b6c9e6b3f76dd845a38941188e6b65947d56130eac4c9bd9f595d; FEMMPA 1995 s.17(2)

claims.subject: Domiciliary opening source-disclosure obligation (statutory exception)
claims.rule: Except as provided under any other enactment or law, a person making an application to open a domiciliary account under this Act shall not be obliged to disclose the source of the foreign currency sought to be deposited in the account
claims.scope: application to open domiciliary account under FEMMPA; statutory exception retained; not a no-KYC / no-AML absolute
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-003; reviewed fingerprint sha256:0d9476fd9070b159a27bb90078e709f6980fc6661b988f85cdcd6eb74119ced9; FEMMPA 1995 s.17(3); project status bounded under negative-claim discipline despite M2.5 supported
allowed_wording: shall not be obliged to disclose the source
Except as provided under any other enactment or law

claims.subject: Multiple domiciliary accounts
claims.rule: A person may open more than one domiciliary account under this Act designated in the same or different foreign currencies and at the same or in different banks
claims.scope: multiple domiciliary-account entitlement only
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-004; reviewed fingerprint sha256:389bf23f93b6878bd29296c7260e162fbecb9a5ba135a18ea95bcf81bdc79b6d; FEMMPA 1995 s.17(4)

claims.subject: Exporter foreign-currency domiciliary account for export proceeds
claims.rule: An exporter of goods, including petroleum products, shall open and maintain a foreign currency domiciliary account into which may be retained foreign currency corresponding to the entire proceeds of the export concerned
claims.scope: exporter of goods including petroleum products; export-proceeds domiciliary account; distinct from ordinary domiciliary
claims.authority: Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1995
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-005; reviewed fingerprint sha256:6fc71368f1f0a19a60619984136fd971e90b268599e0015f25f34ae481c7030e; FEMMPA 1995 s.19; exporter class only
forbidden_inferences: exporter rules apply to ordinary domiciliary accounts
collapsing exporter and ordinary domiciliary classes
export domiciliary cash-withdrawal restriction from unpinned Manual

claims.subject: External-account eligible classes (CDD Reg. 25)
claims.rule: For external and non-resident non-Nigerian customers, financial institutions shall satisfy themselves that the customer is permanently resident outside Nigeria, and the eligible classes for external accounts are embassies, high commissions, legations or consulates, their career and established members, and other international organisations recognised and accorded diplomatic status and their expatriate officials
claims.scope: external accounts; diplomatic / international-organisation classes only
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria — Customer Due Diligence Regulations, 2023
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-006; reviewed fingerprint sha256:80d3285913e428f147e8683e58660d17b2c5e00d8b0345ee8bb0318c57afbab5; CDD Reg. 25(1)-(2)
forbidden_inferences: non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: Non-resident-account eligible classes (CDD Reg. 25)
claims.rule: The eligible classes to open non-resident accounts under the CBN Customer Due Diligence Regulations are overseas correspondence and examination bodies, foreign companies executing approved contracts in Nigeria, and foreign professional bodies
claims.scope: enumerated non-resident-account classes only; not all non-residents
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria — Customer Due Diligence Regulations, 2023
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-007; reviewed fingerprint sha256:372b8cdee0a0ef78593ad129273f111206bd8b66e2cd0fab717cffb4910551da; CDD Reg. 25(4)
forbidden_inferences: non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: Closure of CDD Reg. 25(2)/(4) non-resident accounts on completion
claims.rule: All accounts of Non-resident stipulated in subregulations (2) and (4) of regulation 25 of the CBN Customer Due Diligence Regulations, 2023, shall, on completion of the contract or the applicant's business in Nigeria, be closed and the balance on the account, if any, transferred to the customer's account in country of residence, after proper documentation
claims.scope: only accounts under CDD Reg. 25 subregulations (2) and (4); not all non-resident/external accounts
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria — Customer Due Diligence Regulations, 2023
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-008; reviewed fingerprint sha256:05c518a4fd7fba44f37f07a442ad5ed82b7377bdbec41ab00c9a210349250767; uses M2.5 reviewed_text restoring subregulations (2) and (4); project status bounded
allowed_wording: transferred to the customer's account in country of residence
forbidden_inferences: all non-resident accounts automatically close under the same rule
non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: Domiciliary-account customer identification / KYC (CDD Reg. 40)
claims.rule: Where a customer wishes to open a domiciliary account or make a wholesale deposit by cash or inter-bank transfer, a financial institution shall obtain identification evidence appropriate to individuals, companies, or professional intermediaries, and where funding is by inter-bank transfer the institution shall satisfy itself that the transferring institution is regulated for ML, TF or PF prevention in its country of origin
claims.scope: bank customer due diligence / identification for domiciliary opening or wholesale deposit; not CBN prior approval
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria — Customer Due Diligence Regulations, 2023
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-009; reviewed fingerprint sha256:7170cdcb1f2c6984be31862c810ed796d907aafa979a620d0b7803bc0453f9e2; CDD Reg. 40; bank KYC ≠ CBN prior regulatory approval
forbidden_inferences: prior CBN approval required to open domiciliary account
CBN authorisation required for every account
resident FX access prohibited absent CBN approval

claims.subject: Non-Resident Nigerian eligibility for NRNOA / NRNIA
claims.rule: Effective 1 January 2025, eligible Non-Resident Nigerians may own a Non-Resident Nigerian Ordinary Account or a Non-Resident Nigerian Investment Account subject to meeting KYC requirements, without prejudice to Memorandum 17 of the CBN Foreign Exchange Manual (2018)
claims.scope: Non-Resident Nigerians only; NRNOA or NRNIA; KYC; Memo 17 without-prejudice retained
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-010; reviewed fingerprint sha256:1955f84ae10631c72a83ae6faf5638a3b7030db406fb0d89cbbc57cb691949a5; CBN TED NRNOA/NRNIA circular
forbidden_inferences: non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: NRNOA purpose and dual-currency structure
claims.rule: A Non-Resident Nigerian Ordinary Account enables Non-Resident Nigerians to remit their foreign earnings to Nigeria and manage funds in both foreign and local currencies; account holders may maintain both a foreign-currency account and/or a Naira account
claims.scope: NRNOA only; Non-Resident Nigerians; distinct from NRNIA
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-011; reviewed fingerprint sha256:bc57bd6144c3f07fbad1489340403e15e83b8f472854eb4083ddeed03e5bf2b1; NRNOA framework purpose
allowed_wording: foreign-currency account and/or a Naira account
forbidden_inferences: non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: NRNIA purpose and dual-currency structure
claims.rule: A Non-Resident Nigerian Investment Account enables Non-Resident Nigerians to invest in assets in Nigeria in either foreign currency or local currency, and account holders may maintain both a foreign-currency account and/or a Naira account for that purpose
claims.scope: NRNIA only; Non-Resident Nigerians; investment purpose; distinct from NRNOA
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-012; reviewed fingerprint sha256:371e52e4d2ea4a4bfef2f5610c432f471f7993b6b441dd6023aa20f0b58895e1; NRNIA framework purpose
forbidden_inferences: non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: Foreign Exchange Manual Fourth Edition launch (temporal)
claims.rule: On 15 May 2026, the Central Bank of Nigeria officially launched the Fourth Edition of its Foreign Exchange Manual
claims.scope: temporal/framework metadata only; does not establish Manual operational domiciliary rules
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-013; reviewed fingerprint sha256:17d3040396181cd67721ef3139ed6f3fb1a3362489dbdb647d8fc332bea0ff20; governed but unbound — does not bootstrap FX Manual 2026 operational rules
allowed_wording: Fourth Edition of its Foreign Exchange Manual
forbidden_inferences: ordinary vs exporter domiciliary operational restrictions from Manual launch
Form A requirement from Manual launch
export domiciliary cash-withdrawal restriction from Manual launch

claims.subject: CBN clarification referral for unclassified CDD account cases
claims.rule: In cases that are not classified under the external-account or non-resident-account eligible classes in the CBN Customer Due Diligence Regulations, financial institutions shall refer to the Central Bank of Nigeria for clarification
claims.scope: unclassified / outside-listed CDD cases only; not universal non-resident CBN approval
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria — Customer Due Diligence Regulations, 2023
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-014; reviewed fingerprint sha256:950ffca18f7c45078f29286e1228b2ea973481269517b6c093e04e240b63c2c9; CDD Reg. 25(8)
allowed_wording: not classified under the external-account or non-resident-account eligible classes
refer to the Central Bank of Nigeria for clarification
forbidden_inferences: all non-resident accounts require CBN approval
non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: NRNOA foreign-currency balance repatriation
claims.rule: Balances in the foreign-currency account of a Non-Resident Nigerian Ordinary Account can be fully repatriated out of Nigeria without restriction
claims.scope: NRNOA foreign-currency account balances only; not NRNIA, not all non-resident funds, not resident domiciliary
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-015; reviewed fingerprint sha256:c81067bb6e0446b5f5f323964acfd6047d9625956de1a4f043be7386acf9e6be; NRNOA framework 1.4; literal primary repatriation wording retained with hard anti-expansion forbids
allowed_wording: fully repatriated out of Nigeria without restriction
forbidden_inferences: all non-resident funds are freely repatriable
all investor capital is freely repatriable
resident domiciliary balances are freely transferable
non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval

claims.subject: NRNOA Naira account funding / conversion channel
claims.rule: Non-Resident Nigerian Ordinary Account holders may maintain a Naira account with funds remitted directly from offshore or convertible from a foreign-currency account at prevailing exchange rates through authorised dealers
claims.scope: NRNOA-specific Naira funding/conversion via authorised dealers; not a general local-funding rule
claims.authority: Central Bank of Nigeria
claims.matching_source_note: Adopted from CC-NG-ACC-016; reviewed fingerprint sha256:396160782e6ba8dfda9a48d1f82486d7424a22df3677c2b91e195a507566ed2e; NRNOA currency/conversion limb
forbidden_inferences: unrestricted local deposits for all account classes
non-residents may open and operate FCY accounts
all non-resident accounts require CBN approval
